query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) and high-entropy ceramics with improved mechanical properties, thermal stability, and resistance to oxidation. Various fabrication methods have been explored, including mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and reactive spark plasma sintering. The addition of elements such as Zr, Ti, and Nb has been shown to enhance the properties of HEAs. However, challenges remain in achieving uniform microstructures, controlling grain growth, and minimizing contamination.
decision.unsolved: Despite significant progress, there are still challenges to be addressed in the development of high-entropy alloys and ceramics, including achieving uniform microstructures, controlling grain growth, and minimizing contamination. Additionally, the high-entropy alloys and ceramics often exhibit complex phase structures, which can be difficult to predict and control.
decision.why: Reactive spark plasma sintering has been shown to be an effective method for synthesizing high-entropy alloys and ceramics with improved properties. This method allows for the in-situ formation of desired phases and can help to minimize contamination. By optimizing the processing conditions, such as the spark plasma sintering temperature and time, it may be possible to achieve uniform microstructures and control grain growth, leading to improved mechanical properties and thermal stability.
